name: Pipeliners - Site Speed Audit and Tracker 2026-07-14
body:
> Audit · Pipeliners · 2026-07-14

# Summary
Two linked files: `pipeliners-sitespeed-audit-2026-07-14.md` (read-only audit written for Scott) and `pipeliners-sitespeed-tracker.md` (a living homepage tracker that ties each slow PageSpeed metric to its cause and logs scores).

# Audit findings
- It corrects the July 13 audit: images were already served as WebP (hero about 52 KB), so "16.9 MB of unoptimized images" was wrong.
- Real causes: every LiteSpeed page optimization was OFF (23 stylesheets and 22 scripts unminified and undeferred) and three oversized homepage videos (37.5 + 18.1 + 11.3 MB = 66.9 MB).
- LiteSpeed Cache is the right plugin for Hostinger; do not buy WP Rocket.
- Fix order: safe toggles first (CSS/JS/HTML minify, font-display swap, image and iframe lazy-load), compress videos with poster images, test combine/defer/critical CSS one at a time, final mobile retest. `wp-content/uploads` holds 499 MB of `.bk` backup copies (disk only, not served).

# Tracker log
- Baseline Jul 14: mobile 21, desktop 55; LCP 6.9s, TBT 1,670 ms, CLS 0.331, SI 9.3s.
- After Phase 1 toggles: mobile 45; CLS 0.331 to 0.001, TBT to 850 ms, but LCP regressed to 9.4s (lazy-load delaying the hero).
- Phase 2: videos 67 MB to 19 MB (720 wide, audio stripped), in-place swap, Hostinger CDN flushed; poster images not added.
- Later lesson recorded in the handoff: JS Minify broke the pixfort footer and stays OFF. The case study reports mobile PSI 21 to 43 overall.
